q: What fraction of the paper's original 2022 PGAP CDS annotations survived the 2026 GenBank re-annotation, and are the differences (delta ranging -127 to +360 across the 7 sequences) explainable as pseudogene/short-ORF reclassification vs. genuine locus split/merge?
basis: Our re-count of CDS features from live NCBI EFetch of CP078106..CP078112 (2026-07-06) yields CDS counts that differ from Negrete et al. Table 1 (2022 PGAP) by -127 (H322 chromosome), +360 (GK1025B chromosome), -23 (pH322_1), -11 (pH322_2), -18 (pGK1025B_1), -22 (pGK1025B_2), -21 (pGK1025B_3). All 7 lengths and GC% match exactly, so the reference contigs are identical; only the annotation layer drifted. This is a real reproducibility issue for any BVBRC replication that relies on published Table-1 CDS counts as a testable claim.
next_steps: Pull the paper-era (2022-06) annotation snapshot from the NCBI genome archive (ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCA/019/930/xxx/all_assembly_versions/). Diff CDS coordinate sets against current 2026 annotation. Classify each delta as merge / split / new / removed / pseudogene reclassification. Report per-genome annotation-stability metric. This directly informs whether historical BVBRC papers using PGAP CDS counts are safe to cite verbatim in 2026.

q: Where does the actual SSU5 prophage begin and end inside pH322_1 and pGK1025B_1, and why does direct nucleotide BLAST cover only 57-67% of SSU5 while PHASTER scored the prophage as 'intact ~96.9 Kbp'?
basis: Our BLAST of NC_018843 (Salmonella phage SSU5, 104,828 bp) against CP078111 (pH322_1) gave 21 HSPs merging to 56.6% qcov; against CP078107 (pGK1025B_1), 22 HSPs merging to 67.0% qcov. Both at 80-91% nucleotide identity. PHASTER's 'intact 96.9 Kbp' score is presence-of-phage-genes-based, not raw nucleotide coverage, so the two numbers are not directly comparable — but the paper leaves the actual prophage boundary implicit.
next_steps: Run PHASTEST (open-source PHASTER successor, https://phastest.ca) or DBSCAN-SWA (CLI-friendly) on CP078111 and CP078107 with default settings; extract the reported prophage att-site coordinates. Overlay against our BLAST HSP coverage tracks. Report the 'phage-encoded genes' region vs 'phage-nucleotide-homology' region delta for both plasmids. This clarifies whether pCS1-family phage-plasmids carry accessory (non-SSU5) cargo inside the PHASTER prophage boundary.

q: Is pGK1025B_3 actually transfer-competent (functionally conjugative) or does the T4SS gene cluster merely encode a non-functional/incomplete conjugation apparatus?
basis: The paper claims pGK1025B_3 is a 'novel conjugative Cronobacter plasmid' on the strength of a ~16.4 Kbp T4SS locus. Our annotation-parse of CP078109 confirmed virB3, virB4, virB9, virB10, virB11, a conjugative relaxase, and phospholipase D — but no wet-lab conjugation was reported. T4SS presence is necessary but not sufficient for conjugation; many plasmid T4SS clusters are pseudogenized or missing essential *dtr* or *trbC* components.
next_steps: Wet-lab biparental mating assay: GK1025B (donor, chromosomal spec/streptomycin marker) x rifampin-resistant E. coli K-12 recipient (or C. sakazakii cured of pGK1025B_3 as recipient). Overnight mating on filter, select on selective+counterselective media, PCR-confirm pGK1025B_3 marker (e.g. virB11 or unique phospholipase D allele) in transconjugants. Compute conjugation frequency. Alternative in-silico step first: scan pGK1025B_3 for canonical *oriT* motifs and TraI/relaxase active-site residues using MOB-typer.

q: Does the arsC/arsA/arsB arsenic-resistance operon on pH322_2 and pGK1025B_2 measurably increase arsenic tolerance in H322 and GK1025B, or is it a silent legacy operon?
basis: Paper reports the arsenic operon as shared with pSP291_1 and pESA3 but on annotation grounds only — no phenotypic data. Our GenBank inspection of CP078108 and CP078112 confirmed arsC (x2), arsA/arsB efflux transporter annotations. In many enteric plasmids the arsenic operon is transcriptionally silent under normal conditions and only induced by trace arsenite.
next_steps: MIC / MBC assay panel with NaAsO2 (arsenite, As(III)) and Na2HAsO4 (arsenate, As(V)) across a concentration series (0.01-10 mM) for: (1) wild-type H322, (2) wild-type GK1025B, (3) plasmid-cured H322 (pH322_2-), (4) plasmid-cured GK1025B (pGK1025B_2-), (5) an arsC::kan knockout in each background. Also RT-qPCR of arsC induction after 30-min arsenite spike. Compare against a C. sakazakii reference strain (BAA-894) that lacks the operon.

q: Should the CGE PlasmidFinder Enterobacteriales database add a Cronobacter-specific replicon family — and if so, what are the representative repA sequences that should seed it?
basis: Our re-run of PlasmidFinder-BLAST at CGE defaults (95% id + 60% qcov) confirmed the paper's claim of 0 hits for all 5 plasmids. Best hits were 80.2-91.5% identity — meaningfully homologous but below the reporting threshold. This means CGE PlasmidFinder is systematically blind to Cronobacter plasmids of clinical/food-safety interest. Since there are now ~50 closed C. sakazakii plasmids in GenBank, a curated Cronobacter replicon set is tractable.
next_steps: (1) Programmatically extract every closed C. sakazakii plasmid (~50-100 sequences) from NCBI. (2) Predict repA (replication initiator) regions with iterons+CDS-annotation heuristics. (3) Cluster repA sequences with CD-HIT-EST at 95%/90%/80% identity; enumerate replicon families. (4) Cross-reference to any already-named Cronobacter replicons (pCS1, pESA3, pSP291_1, and the 5 in this paper). (5) Submit a curated 'plasmidfinder_cronobacter.fsa' contribution to the CGE Bitbucket repo. Directly closes a reproducibility gap this replication surfaced.
